Dated this the 4th day of February, 2026
JUDGMENT

This appeal arises out of the reference filed under Section 30 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act,
1984.
2.

An extent of 3475 square meters of land in different survey numbers was acquired by the referring officer for the purpose of constructing the C.C. Road connecting Thiruvathapalli to Eastern Jetty,
Kavaratti Island, after notification dated 1.1.2010 under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation, fixing the market value at Rs.3,436/- per square meter.
At the time of the disbursement of the compensation, a dispute arose as regards 20 square meters of land in Survey No.675/1B.
Thereafter, the claim was referred under Section 30 read with Section 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act.

The claimants 1 to 5 supported the claim,
whereas claimants 6 to 9 disputed the claim and claimed rights based on Exts.B1 and B2.
L.A.A. No.641 of 2015 4 2026:KER:10255

According to them, the property is a Tharawad property,
for which, they are also entitled to claim compensation.

The claimants 1 to 5, on the other hand,
contended that there was an oral partition in the year 1952 and, in O.S. No.7 of 1998 before the District Court, Kavaratti, there was a prayer to set aside document Nos.61/1997 and 62/1997,
wherein the plea of oral partition in the year 1952 was upheld.

Accordingly, accepting the said judgment and decree, the reference was answered in favour of the claimants 1 to 5 and hence the present appeal by the claimants 6 to 9.
3.

In this appeal, it is the specific case of the appellants that the property in question is still a Tharawad property and that the judgment and decree in O.S. No.7 of 1998 has not become final,
especially since A.S. No.212 of 2002 is pending on the files of this Court.

4. Heard Sri. Joby Jacob Pulickekudy, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant and Sri. K.S.
Prenjith Kumar, the learned Central Government Counsel appearing for the 1st respondent.
5.
On consideration of the submissions raised across the bar, L.A.A. No.641 of 2015 5 2026:KER:10255 this Court finds that by judgment dated 15.1.2016, A.S. No.217 of 2002 was dismissed for default.
No attempts have been made by the appellants therein to have the appeal restored, and a decision be invited on merits.
Therefore, as on today, the judgment and decree in O.S. No.7 of 1998 has become final.
6. It is further contended that the judgment and decree in O.S. No.7 of 1998 has nothing to do with the present claim.
This Court is not impressed by the aforesaid argument.

A perusal of Ext.A10 judgment in O.S. No.7 of 1998 clearly shows that the property in question was involved in the earlier suit and that the court had specifically found that there is an oral partition in respect of the same Muthubi vs The Land Acquisition Collector on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50484913/
3 property which was the subject matter of the land acquisition proceedings.
